title: Jawaharlal Nehru in Ahmednagar Fort: Writing 'The Discovery of India' Behind Bars (1944)
summary: Imprisoned inside the remote Ahmednagar Fort during World War II, Jawaharlal Nehru penned his monumental classic, The Discovery of India, celebrating India's civilizational syncretism.
keywords: Historical Dialogue 181: நேருவும் “நாளை ஓய்வு பெறுவீர்களா?” என்ற தொடர்கேள்வியும்
full_text:
Between August 1942 and March 1945, inside the isolated stone bastions of Ahmednagar Fort in Maharashtra, the British colonial government imprisoned the senior leadership of the Indian National Congress under complete military secrecy.

Among them was Jawaharlal Nehru, enduring his ninth and longest term of imprisonment. Rather than succumbing to despair in the sweltering fortress, Nehru established an unbending daily discipline. In the mornings, he dug into the stony soil of the prison yard to cultivate rose beds; by afternoon, he sat at a simple wooden table, penning thousands of manuscript pages.

His fellow inmate, the brilliant Islamic scholar Maulana Abul Kalam Azad, observed him writing late into the night under a dim electric bulb and asked:
"Jawahar, in this desolate isolation where we know nothing of the war or our release, what captures your spirit with such consuming passion?"

Nehru looked up, his face radiant with inner purpose:
"Maulana, imperial jailers can confine our physical bodies within stone walls, but they cannot imprison the human imagination. I am undertaking a voyage through the centuries to discover the living soul of India!
From the planned brick streets of Mohenjo-daro to the Upanishadic forest academies, and through the synthetic architecture of the Mughals, this subcontinent has absorbed countless cultures without losing its vital spiritual center. India is an ancient palimpsest upon which layer after layer of thought has been inscribed without erasing what went before. I am writing 'The Discovery of India' so that when our people step into freedom, they will do so with profound self-respect and pride in their pluralistic civilizational heritage!"

Written entirely within the confines of Ahmednagar Fort, The Discovery of India became a classic of world literature and the intellectual charter of modern democratic India.
